scientific_hypothesis: A source-side cycle score normalized by a conservative representative-point uncertainty scale can retain detection of precise biased skip edges while materially reducing worst-clean false fallback relative to the raw-displacement guard.

primary_candidate.name: representative-point Minkowski-normalized cycle score
primary_candidate.semantics: For each origin/axis representative point, propagate the direct and two path-edge marginal covariances through analytic Sim(3) composition and point Jacobians. Sum the three root expected squared displacement contributions, which is a Minkowski upper bound under arbitrary edge-error cross-correlation. Normalize point disagreement by that bound and aggregate by root mean square.

calibration.source_conditions: clean scenarios only, balanced across registered clean correlation levels
calibration.raw_statistic: maximum representative cycle displacement per trial
calibration.normalized_statistic: maximum uncertainty-normalized cycle score per trial

outlier_semantics.edge_type: direct skip edge with an available directed two-edge path
outlier_semantics.purpose: test detection of an apparently precise but biased source edge

claim_boundary: Controlled synthetic source-cycle admission only; no held-out physical-object provider, BayesianPhysTwin, harmful-update, or Causal4D benefit claim.
